connections.why: The heavy-atom method that Perutz showed in 1953, binding mercury into the protein crystal to give each X-ray reflection its phase, is what let both his hemoglobin and Kendrew's myoglobin be seen.
Perutz's hemoglobin was Bragg's crystallography carried to a molecule of 10,000 atoms, in the Cavendish Laboratory that Lawrence Bragg ran and with his backing for two decades.
